methodological_rigor.justification: The study employs multiple complementary methodologies: 3D spheroid invasion assays in two FNRMS cell lines (RD, SMS-CTR) with an FPRMS control (RH41), ChIP-seq/RNA-seq reanalysis from published datasets, Western blotting with proliferation controls via CellTiter-Glo, IF quantification with MATLAB, pharmacological inhibition (Dooku1, GsMTx4, verteporfin, Y-27632), and patient survival data. Proliferation was controlled to isolate invasion effects. Limitations include reliance on only two FNRMS cell lines without patient-derived models, no genetic knockdown of PIEZO1 to complement pharmacological inhibition, and no in vivo validation. Statistical details are sparse—tests used, sample sizes per condition, and whether multiplicity corrections were applied are not consistently reported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is entirely a preclinical mechanistic study using cell line spheroids and reanalysis of public datasets; Oxford LoE for preclinical work is 5. Clinical relevance is plausible given FNRMS is an aggressive pediatric sarcoma with poor outcomes, and the PIEZO1-survival correlation in the Williamson microarray dataset offers translational hints. However, the pathway targeting uses non-clinically-optimized inhibitors, lacks in vivo efficacy data, and the invasion readout is a spheroid spreading proxy rather than a metastasis model, keeping translation speculative.

reporting_quality.justification: As a preclinical in vitro study, ARRIVE is the most relevant framework, though strictly ARRIVE applies to animal work; many items still apply to rigor reporting. Materials, catalog numbers, and protocols are thoroughly documented enabling replication, but sample sizes, replicate numbers, randomization, blinding, and statistical test specifics are not consistently stated. Public dataset accessions (GSE55186, GSE47198) are given, and the AI-assistance disclosure is present. No explicit data/code availability statement for the newly generated data is included in the text.

novelty_literature.justification: The YAP-PIEZO1 axis has been described in other cancers and PIEZO1-calcium-invasion links are established (refs 19, 28). YAP's role in FNRMS was previously shown by Tremblay et al. (ref 16). The specific contribution—demonstrating ECM-density-driven YAP-PIEZO1 signaling as an invasion axis in FNRMS and identifying PIEZO1 as a direct YAP-TEAD1 transcriptional target in this subtype—is a meaningful extension to a disease-specific context rather than a first-in-class discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with logical flow from phenotype to mechanism to pharmacological validation. Figures are referenced clearly and the narrative builds a coherent model (ECM-YAP-PIEZO1-Ca2+-invasion). Some minor issues include a truncated section heading (3.5 'Spheroid' appears cut), occasional grammatical slips, and technical jargon that could be smoothed, but overall readability is solid.

key_strengths: Integrated mechanistic chain from ECM density to YAP nuclear translocation to direct PIEZO1 transcriptional control (supported by reanalyzed ChIP-seq/RNA-seq) to calcium influx to invasion
Proliferation controls (CellTiter-Glo at 6h) rule out growth as confounder of invasion spreading
Convergent pharmacological evidence using Dooku1, GsMTx4, verteporfin, and Y-27632 strengthens causal inference
Patient-dataset Kaplan-Meier showing PIEZO1-high associated with worse OS adds translational hook
key_concerns: Only two FNRMS cell lines (RD, SMS-CTR) with no patient-derived models, xenograft, or in vivo validation
No genetic loss-of-function (siRNA/shRNA/CRISPR) for PIEZO1 to complement pharmacological inhibition
Statistical reporting is sparse—specific tests, n values, multiplicity correction are inconsistently presented
Novelty is incremental—YAP-PIEZO1 axes and PIEZO1-invasion links are established in other cancers
No explicit data/code availability statement for newly generated imaging and Western blot data
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent, internally consistent mechanistic study with appropriate controls and multi-modal evidence but limited to in vitro spheroid models and with incremental novelty, placing it in Tier 3 with minor revisions to strengthen statistical reporting and data availability.
